newsitem.title: POLAND: CAPITAL INCREASE APPROVED FOR POLISH INSURER PZU.
newsitem.headline: CAPITAL INCREASE APPROVED FOR POLISH INSURER PZU.

text.p: Poland's treasury ministry has approved a share capital increase for state-owned insurer PZU SA ahead of full privatisation, a ministry spokesman said on Wednesday.
Spokesman Zbigniew Ostrowski told Reuters the firm's capital would be increased by between 19.9 and 34 percent through a new stock issue.
PZU, which is Poland's largest insurer, currently has a share capital (at par value) of 60.5 million zlotys.
The management of PZU, Poland's largest insurer, will now draft a list of potential investors and set the terms of the sale which should be completed as soon as possible, Ostrowski said.

"(PZU) management has been obliged to prepare a list of investors including no less than 20 (investors) and not more than 300, including at least five entities carrying out insurance operations," he added.
PZU spokesman Marek Maszek said the new share issue must raise at least 600 million zlotys to guarantee capital adequacy ratios. "We hope it will bring more," he told Reuters.
The government decided last week that PZU, which controls 65 percent of Poland's non-life insurance market and 80 percent of the life market, would be fully privatised next year.
PZU's management has said the privatisation, in which the state holding in company would fall below 50 percent, should take the form of a public offering.

Rejecting opposition allegations that a large stake in the company would be sold cheaply to selected domestic buyers, deputy finance minister Karol Szwarc suggested this year's new share issue could go to foreign investors.
Szwarc told the Rzeczposolita that PZU would benefit from links with West European and U.S. investors.
PZU's Maszek confirmed that the company was in talks with Western investors in connection with the sale.
